text: The key itself is fine -- it's the *sequence* that's the problem. Watch what happens during a failed attempt: `sudo tail -n 30 /var/log/auth.log` after a failed run shows several `Failed publickey for deploy` lines followed by `Disconnecting: Too many authentication failures`.
Every offered key that sshd rejects counts against a per-connection limit, independent of which auth method is used. Check it: `sudo sshd -T | grep -i maxauthtries`.

Find where it's set: `sudo grep -rin maxauthtries /etc/ssh/sshd_config /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/` -- it's `MaxAuthTries 2` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/authtries.conf`. With 2 retired keys offered before the real one, the connection is dropped after the 2nd failure, before the 3rd (correct) key ever gets tried.

Raise the limit high enough to cover the full legitimate sequence, e.g. edit the existing line to `MaxAuthTries 6` (don't just append a second `MaxAuthTries` line to the file -- sshd_config keeps the *first* value it sees for a directive, so an appended duplicate in the same file is silently ignored). Validate and reload: `sudo sshd -t && sudo service ssh reload`.
